title: How Dungeons and Dragons Works
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explain Dungeons and Dragons: its origins in wargaming with Gary Gygax and Dave Arneson, the 1974 release, TSR, the 1977 basic and advanced sets (the Red Box), the Dungeon Master role, character attributes and alignments, dice-based combat and locks, the fractured edition community and fifth edition, the 1979 James Dallas Egbert III disappearance and satanic-panic criticism (including Chick Publications' Dark Dungeons), the 1983 movie, and the cartoon. Also includes a listener mail segment about Larry Elmore's art book.

segments.title: Opening banter and personal D&D experiences
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode and share their childhood experiences playing D&D and other games like Top Secret.

segments.title: Origins: Gary Gygax, Dave Arneson and wargaming
segments.summary: The hosts describe the wargaming roots of D&D, the collaboration between Gary Gygax and Dave Arneson, the chain mail precursor, and the 1974 release.

segments.title: TSR and early editions
segments.summary: They discuss the founding of TSR, the social nature of the game, and the 1977 release of the Basic Set (Red Box) and Advanced Dungeons and Dragons, followed by the 1979 introduction of the DM Guide.

segments.title: Edition changes and fractured community
segments.summary: The hosts cover how each edition changed rules, the resulting fractured fan community, and Wizards of the Coast's fifth edition effort, with Ben Grabowski's skepticism about unifying editions.

segments.title: Character creation, attributes, races and classes
segments.summary: Explanation of the six ability scores, armor class, hit points, and the basic set's character classes (fighter, cleric, magic user, thief, dwarf, halfling, elf), with notes on how each is built.

segments.title: Alignment and alignment tongue
segments.summary: Lawful, chaotic and neutral alignments are described, along with how alignment tongue lets characters of the same alignment speak privately.

segments.title: The Dungeon Master role
segments.summary: The hosts describe the demands of being the Dungeon Master, the caller role, and how turns and group decisions work.

segments.title: Example of play: dungeon, locked door and gelatinous cube
segments.summary: A walk-through example where a thief attempts to pick a lock using a d20 roll, the door hides a gelatinous cube, and combat is resolved with dice and hit points. Experience points and treasure are also discussed.

segments.title: Bags of holding and Baldur's Gate
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the bag of holding and a bag of plenty, and Chuck's mention of Baldur's Gate and where to find local D&D groups.

segments.title: D&D Online and satanic panic
segments.summary: The hosts mention D&D Online, then describe the 1979 disappearance of James Dallas Egbert III and the satanic panic criticism of D&D, including Chick Publications' Dark Dungeons.

segments.title: Movies, cartoon and female players
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Tom Hanks movie, the failure of a D&D movie to satisfy fans, the cartoon, and a documentary noting female players.

segments.title: Sponsor break and listener mail intro
segments.summary: Brief transition and sponsor read for Jack Threads.

segments.title: Listener mail: Larry Elmore art book
segments.summary: A listener, Jeremy Elmore, writes that his father Larry Elmore, a freelance artist who painted for TSR, is sending the hosts copies of his art book.
